item.title: Understanding behavior in real-world contexts
item.content:encoded:
Dolores Albarracin, University of Pennsylvania

Mandy Hütter, University of Zurich

Zachary A. Niese, Montclair State University

This special section seeks research that bridges laboratory-based psychological science with real-world contexts and consequential behavior. While researchers have identified many important psychological processes, much existing work isolates these processes from the social and ecological environments where they actually operate. The special section aims to advance understanding of how psychological processes function within the environments people inhabit and their relationship to behavior that matters beyond the research setting.

Appel publié par Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Environmental properties and psychological processes
  • Informational, institutional, and cultural environments
  • Physical environments and behavior
  • Psychological processes and real-world behavior
  • Person-environment transactions
  • Beliefs and attitudes in context
  • Memory and consequential outcomes

Associate editors

  • Nick Butrick, University of Washington
  • Oliver Sng, National University of Singapore

item.title: Close Relationships in an Interdependent Social World
item.content:encoded:
Sandra Murray, University at Buffalo

Are close relationships in peril? Loneliness is increasing and markers of social engagement (e.g., marriage) are decreasing. This special section hopes to provide insight into this question by tackling the socially nested nature of interdependence itself.

Close relationships with significant others take place in the broader context of family responsibilities, such as those involved in parenting children and caring for aging parents; in the broader context of friendship networks, and broader communities; in the context of sociopolitical pressures, such as economic stress, racism, and political polarization; and in the context of technological changes, such as those posed by the insertion of AI into social life.

Appel publié par Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How contextual or socially nested nature of interdependence shapes close relationship dynamics
  • Relationship dynamics relevant to relationship initiation, maintenance, or dissolution
  • Close relationships in the broader context of family responsibilities (parenting children, caring for aging parents)
  • Close relationships in the broader context of friendship networks and communities
  • Close relationships in the context of sociopolitical pressures (economic stress, racism, political polarization)
  • Close relationships in the context of technological changes (AI insertion into social life)
